questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to go to Italy due to the people and culture there.

questions.answer: Pretty easy. The international mobility office were very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Pretty easy, if you are willing to pay for more expensive accommodation. 
I booked a room in a shared apartment by Joivy through Spot a Home. Overall, it was a good experience. Unimi has an agreement with Spot a Home where you can get a 25% discount on administrative fees, so make sure to check that out in advance. You can also book directly with Joivy (then you have less administrative fees), however Spot a Home says they protect your deposit.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Live close to the center, it is more expensive, but since you are there for a short time it is worth all the money (and more safe).

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Course registration opens quite late compared to the University of Copenhagen. So have patience. And you can register to courses after they have started. It can therefore be a good idea to go check out different classes in the first weeek or two to figure out what you like.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can read about the different courses online, write the professors if you have any questions, or write the international mobility office if you have any practical issues or questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very. I got all the classes I wanted. I don't think they have a limit on how many people can participate in the classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go check out many different courses in the first week as they can be quite different from their online description.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the classes really interesting and very different from the University if Copenhagen.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All my courses were at MA level, and where not that difficult (easier than the University of Copenhagen).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was smaller classes, attendance, and more active participation. I also had presentations in almost all of my classes. On the other hand the curriculum was a lot smaller.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
I took two trimesters. 

At the first trimester I had: "Global Challenges to Democracy", "History and Politics of North Africa and the Middle East" & "Workshop: Human Trafficking/Smuggling". 

At the second trimester I had: "Contemporary Challenges: Migrations and Cultural Diversity", "Contemporary Challenges: Labor Market and Inequalities" & "Asylum from the Field: Borders, Struggles, and Integration Practices".

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
My favourite class was "Workshop: Human Trafficking/Smuggling". It was really interesting, very different from what we learn at the University of Copenhagen, and the professor was really good. 
I also really liked the class "History and Politics of North Africa and the Middle East", however it is a lot of history. And the professor of the class "Contemporary Challenges: Labor Market and Inequalities" was also really good.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I decided to travel in Italy a lot, which I used a lot of money on.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee and eggs are very cheap. In general it is cheaper to go out than in Denmark, but more expensive than the rest of Italy, and not that cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't attend any. However, I think erasmus plans many different events that you can attend. I attended a few, and it is a good way to meet new people.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know, I didn't attend any.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't attend any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go travel. There is a lot of places you can easily access from Milan. Go see the lakes, Liguria, etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy as Milan is a more international/European city.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend classes alone (without other Danish exchange students). That was how I met most of my international friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: In the beginning I found it difficult to adjust to the different administrative system. However, over time it was fine. The exams are also a bit different, but again it was fine once you had tried it a first time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and more laid back attitude - being able to enjoy the everyday life more.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't panic if you get all of your information last minute, it is all going to be fine.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The international mobility office are very kind and helpfull, so write them an email if you have any issues.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and cultures.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably some unexpected practical issues with our apartment, but it all worked out.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just enjoy it and don't be afraid to speak to new people :-)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
